questions.text: Why decouple visual encoding for understanding and generation in a Janus-style model?

options.A: To prevent the two tasks from sharing any transformer parameters.
options.B: To make semantic image embeddings directly reversible into exact pixels.
options.C: To avoid using a visual decoder when producing generated images.
options.D: To use semantic features for understanding and reconstruction-oriented codes for generation.

questions.explanation: Understanding and generation benefit from different visual representations. Separate encoding paths serve those goals while retaining a shared transformer body.

questions.text: In a Janus-Pro-style generation path, the transformer has predicted image VQ code IDs. What produces the image pixels?

options.A: A text tokenizer converts the IDs into a natural-language caption.
options.B: The VQ decoder reconstructs an image from the generated codes.
options.C: The semantic encoder treats each ID as a class label and returns pixels.
options.D: The router averages all code IDs into one RGB color.

questions.explanation: The VQ generation path predicts codebook IDs, and its visual decoder renders those codes into an image.

questions.text: The toy router counts matching understanding and generation keywords and returns ambiguous on a tie. What does route("Sketch a cat and then describe its breed") return?

options.C: ambiguous, because each keyword group matches once.
options.D: generate, because generation takes precedence on ties.

questions.explanation: Sketch contributes one generation match and describe one understanding match. The scores tie, so the function returns ambiguous.
